facts: The **hypotenuse** is the longest side, the one opposite the right angle.
The hypotenuse is the same side whichever acute angle you work from.
The **opposite** side is the side across the triangle from the marked angle; it does not touch that angle.
The **adjacent** side is the side that touches the marked angle and is **not** the hypotenuse.
The hypotenuse touches the marked angle too, so touching the angle is not enough to make a side the adjacent side.
A side may be named by a single pronumeral ($p$) or by its two end vertices ($PQ$, the same side as $QP$).
steps: Find the hypotenuse, opposite the right angle
Find the opposite side, across from the marked angle
Name the remaining side the adjacent side

foundation.solution_text:
Side $h$ lies opposite the right angle.
It is the hypotenuse.

Side $n$ does not touch $\theta$; it lies across the triangle from it.
It is the opposite side.

Side $v$ touches $\theta$ and is not the hypotenuse ($w$ is).
It is the adjacent side.

The hypotenuse is $e$, opposite the right angle at $X$.
The side across the triangle from $\theta$ is $d$.

The hypotenuse is $n$, so it cannot be the adjacent side.
The other side touching $\theta$ is $k$.

The hypotenuse is $YZ$, opposite the right angle at $X$.
The side across the triangle from $\theta$ is $XY$.

The hypotenuse is $PR$, so it cannot be the adjacent side.
The other side touching $\theta$ is $PQ$.

development.solution_text:
Opposite $\theta$: $h$
Opposite $\alpha$: $g$
Moving the reference angle swaps the two shorter sides over.

The hypotenuse is $v$, so it is never the adjacent side.
Adjacent to $\theta$: $s$
Adjacent to $\alpha$: $t$

The hypotenuse is $w$, opposite the right angle.
Side $n$ does not touch $\theta$, so it is the opposite side.

The hypotenuse is $d$, opposite the right angle at $K$.
The side across the triangle from $\theta$ is $c$.

The hypotenuse is $g$, so it cannot be the adjacent side.
The other side touching $\theta$ is $e$.

mastery.solution_text:
Opposite $\theta$ and adjacent to $\alpha$: $y$
Opposite $\alpha$ and adjacent to $\theta$: $x$
The hypotenuse $z$ takes neither role, for either angle.

Hypotenuse for $\theta$: $PR$
Hypotenuse for $\alpha$: $PR$
The hypotenuse is fixed by the right angle at $Q$, not by the reference angle, so it is the same side for both.
